Hi Sarah / Neha — thanks for the note. I’m Vivek (Head of Security & Compliance). Quick answers and what's attached.

Summary answers: 
- Our most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers the period 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31 and was issued 2026-01-20. We can provide the PDF under NDA; I’ve noted it as requested in attachments.

- Subservice organizations: Redwood leverages AWS (primary compute and storage) and a secondary provider (GCP) for some non-production analytics workloads. We treat AWS as a primary subservice org for production controls. Our SOC report references reliance on AWS SOC reports for certain infrastructure-level controls — those are noted as carve-outs in the SOC narrative where the cloud provider performs the control. For example, physical access and hypervisor-level controls are not re-tested at Redwood.

- Controls testing and scope: For controls that rely on AWS SOC, our auditors validated that we have compensating controls where needed (e.g., IAM policies, network segregation, host hardening, encryption at rest keys under our KMS). The SOC report includes descriptions of which common controls are in-scope vs. carved out. If you need the specific control IDs (e.g., CC6, CC7 mappings) we can extract a short mapping sheet.

- Subprocessors: attached is an inventory CSV (subprocessors_inventory.csv) showing vendors, service, region, and in-scope date. Key entries: AWS (us-east-1) in scope since 2022-06-01; GCP (us-west-2) used for analytics since 2024-09-15; Datadog (monitoring) since 2023-03-10.

- Bridge letter: yes, we can provide a bridge letter to attest to control continuity between the end of the audit period and your effective procurement date. We typically limit bridge letters to a 6-month window beyond the SOC report date unless otherwise negotiated. I’ll attach a bridge_letter_template.docx for your review.

Attachments included (stubs in this thread):
- subprocessors_inventory.csv (full inventory)
- bridge_letter_template.docx (standard language)
- SOC2_Redwood_Inference_TypeII_2025.pdf (available upon NDA)

Notes / caveats: 
- AWS/GCP SOC reports: we can provide the relevant cloud provider report URLs/guidance. Cloud provider reports are issued to customers via their respective portals (e.g., AWS Artifact) and we do not host vendor SOC PDFs. If Acme requires copies, your security team will need access to the provider portal or we can provide the exact report IDs and the date ranges so your security team can request them from AWS/GCP or we can coordinate with your security contact to get them.

- Carve-outs vs. inclusive: our SOC report is not a full carve-in of all cloud controls; some controls remain the responsibility of the cloud provider and are documented as such. Operational controls that Redwood performs (e.g., deployment change control, access provisioning, application logging) were tested at Redwood by the auditor.

3) We will produce a Bridge Letter draft for Acme to sign/acknowledge within 5 business days.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute joint call with our auditors on the mapping for a deeper dive.
